releases.body:
### Changed

- Bumped `@opencode/client` to 2.2.5.
- Verified with OpenCode V2 2.2.5.

### Security

- Bumped `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` to 0.8.1 and `solid-js` to
  1.9.18. A consumer install now gets `seroval` 1.6.12, past
  GHSA-97r2-qh9m-474h, GHSA-wp97-x4hv-qvhp, GHSA-7rv5-mrxv-xcr9,
  GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c and GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp, and `@babel/core` 7.29.7, past
  GHSA-4x5r-pxfx-6jf8. The consumer `npm audit` gate no longer admits any
  residual advisory.

### Fixed

- Commands that usually only read are no longer labeled read-only when they
  write or run something. `sort` now recognizes `-o` inside a short-option
  cluster (`sort -uo FILE`), attached (`-nruoFILE`), and as an abbreviated
  long option (`--out=FILE`), and `--compress-program` as code execution.
  `uniq` and `xxd` now report their second operand as a write, `tree` reports
  `-o FILE` and `-R`, and `yq` reports `-i` inside a cluster (`-iP`) and
  `--inplace=true`. Before, enforced policy rules on writes or code execution
  did not match these forms, and the reviewer was told the command was
  read-only.
- On OpenCode V2, the TUI's fallback theme is a fresh copy on every call, so a
  caller that mutates the returned theme no longer changes it for later
  renders.

### Changed

- The minimum Bun is now 1.3.14 (`engines.bun`), the floor declared by
  `@opentui/core` 0.8. Every supported OpenCode host already embeds Bun 1.3.14
  or later, so plugin installs inside OpenCode are unaffected. CI now runs
  1.3.14 and 1.4.4.
- Verified with OpenCode V1 1.19.5.

### Added

- Liquid AI `liquid-ai/d1` and `liquid-ai/d1-ultra` as System One reviewer
  models, with the key read from `LIQUID_API_KEY`. A key that is not shaped
  like a Liquid AI key (`liquid_` prefix) is never sent; the review follows the
  failure settings instead. Liquid keys are also redacted from reviewer evidence
  (#94, thanks @giannisCKS). On the synthetic benchmark, `liquid-ai/d1-ultra` is
  recommended and `liquid-ai/d1` is not; see the README for its settings.
- Baseten's mammoth-1 and elephant-1 decision models as System One reviewer
  models (`baseten/decision-models/baseten-mammoth-27b-latest` and
  `baseten/decision-models/baseten-elephant-9b-latest`), with the key read from
  `BASETEN_API_KEY`.
- The README's TypeSafe AI route now names `typesafe-ai/jev-1.14.0`, the release
  evaluated on the synthetic benchmark.

### Fixed

- OpenCode session IDs in reviewer evidence (intent, actor, and lineage) are no
  longer masked as credentials, so the reviewer can tell which session each
  piece of intent came from. Other values assigned to session keys are still
  redacted.
- On OpenCode V2, package script evidence starts from the shell command's
  `workdir`, resolving relative paths against the session directory, instead of
  always using the session directory. The `workdir` is followed to its real
  path, as package managers do, and one that is not an existing directory marks
  the scripts as unresolved rather than reporting another manifest. Reads stay
  within the approved evidence roots.

### Changed

- Bumped the `@opencode/client` runtime dependency to 2.1.4.
- Bumped the `zod` runtime dependency to 4.6.7.
- Verified with OpenCode V1 1.19.4 and V2 2.1.3.

### Fixed

- On OpenCode V2, run reviews with the model's own default when the reviewer
  model does not offer the built-in `medium` variant. Models without variants,
  such as `opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash`, previously made every review fail
  closed. An explicitly configured variant the model lacks still fails closed,
  and the reason now lists the variants the model offers.

### Changed

- Bumped the `@opencode/client` runtime dependency to 2.0.28, which moves
  `effect` from 4.0.0-rc.112 to the stable 4.0.1.
- Verified with OpenCode V1 1.19.0 and V2 2.0.28.
- Documented that free OpenCode Zen models cannot act as the reviewer: Zen
  rejects the sessions the plugin creates, so every review falls back to a
  manual prompt.

### Fixed

- Keep MCP servers out of the OpenCode V1 reviewer location when plugins from
  config sources applied after it (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`,
  `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, the global plugin directory) add them from their config
  hooks. Those servers previously started inside the reviewer location and made
  every review fail closed.
